title: Early big-map fold behind a shedding king: on 1152+ tiles the king beacon and final fold start at P.bigFoldRound (300), stacked on I427's shedding king
hypothesis: Pre-mortem finding (this review): we most likely lose the Grand Final at round 500 on big unseen maps, because the leaders' king is far longer than ours while our total length would beat it: in 8023's 10 online round-500 losses their longest was 43.5 against our 22.7, and our fold-all bound beat their longest in 8 (95% 49-94%); 7676 in 19 of 26. Our king is short when the fold starts: 6.7 long at r396 in this review's rule counts (the longest 10.9), and grows about 18 by r499 (9.3 from pearls, 12.9 from 3+ merges); a king eats at most one pearl a move, so its length at the fold's start and the rounds left decide it. The leaders start earlier and from longer: rank 2's 336660 longest 22 at r350, 40 at r400; rank 1's 343541 13 at r350, 40 at r450. E0151 (I302) tried the r300 fold on 1152+ tiles: the king led at r400 (31.6 v 19.2) and short rammers killed it (34-38 king deaths from r300 in 24 games; swarm 18/24 v 22/24, p 0.06; breeder 9 v 16, p about 0.03). What it depended on has changed: E0157's shed now cuts threatened long dragons' head-on deaths by 70-90% before r397, and I427 extends it to the king through the fold. Change, behind P.bigEarlyFold: where W*H >= P.bigFoldArea (1152, as E0132's reserve), beaconRound and foldRound become P.bigFoldRound (300), and threatShedEnd follows for non-kings; smaller maps unchanged. Built on I427's candidate as a stack (MISSES 21): measured alone, E0151 said the early king dies; with the shedding king the question is whether it survives. Choices: scope = maps of 1152+ tiles; E0167's local fold (2400+, foldReach 12) stays, so distant dragons keep breeding; what counts as a loss = the king's length at r499 and the king's deaths by cause. Siblings: I410 (early fold on walled maps only, by the echo-kelp observable), I312 (feeding the king at the cap from r250), I307 (earlyking's port, r275/r280 everywhere). Measure first on the logging copy (6 fresh 1152+ maps, both sides, against swarm and breeder): king deaths from r300 against E0151's 34-38 in 24 games; stop only if they are not lower at sign p <= 0.1 over matched map-sides (chance.sign_p); otherwise build. Fire rate: every dragon's fold decision on 1152+ maps from r300 (rule counts: fold set on 4.1% of logged turns on 1025-2399 tiles and 7.7% on 2400+ today, from r397). Scenarios: (1) a 48x48 map at r305: the longest reports as king and dragons within reach fold. (2) Boundary: 32x32 (1024 tiles): no change. (3) A threatened king at r350 sheds (I427) and its child is heir. Report the per-size scores and the king's length at r400 and r499.

title: The near-ceiling king hold on every map size: within P.kingHoldLead slots of the ordinary-split ceiling, our king holds its ordinary splits on maps under 1152 tiles too
hypothesis: General quantity: our king line's length at r396 (the end of r396; tools/replays.py king_at_fold) against the opponent's in round-500 losses. E0203 (I441, kept at +9.1, H1, 1236 pairs) makes the king hold its ordinary splits and farm trips on maps of 1152+ tiles, either while the team is within P.kingHoldLead slots of where ordinary splits stop or from P.kingSeedRound. Its trials gained on 1152+ tiles (0.520, n 901) and not on smaller maps, where only its fold-window farm skip acts (0.496, n 335; paired z between the two 2.56). The same gap exists on small maps online: in 8636's <=1024-tile r500 losses our king at r396 was 2.6 against their 9.2 (their king longer in 11 of 12, sign p 0.0005), and in 8473's 2.9 against 16.2 (11 of 12, p 0.0005). The near-ceiling half of the hold is not about map size. When the team is within P.kingHoldLead slots of unitLimit - rescueReserve(w), another dragon's split refills a freed slot within a round or two, so the king's child adds no unit on any map. It only moves P.childLength off the king. The area gate stood in for the chance of elimination (all 14 of 7003's elimination losses were on <=1024 tiles), but a team at its ceiling is not short of units. Change, behind its own switch P.kingHoldNearCeilingAnySize: kingSeedOn's near-ceiling clause applies on every map size. The r300 fallback clause (w.round >= P.kingSeedRound) stays gated on P.kingSeedArea, and so do the king report before the beacon and splitOutHeir's early branch where they come from that clause. On small maps rescueReserve is 0, so the ceiling is unitLimit and the hold starts at unitLimit - P.kingHoldLead. Scenarios: 32x32 at r200 with 62 of 64 units, the king holds its ordinary split and skips a pearl pocket. The same board with 61 units splits as today. A trapped king still splits out. At r320 with 40 units on 32x32 nothing changes (the fallback stays big-only). Choices: holder = every dragon isKing picks. E0203's debug games (32 on big maps) put 5-10 such dragons a round before r405, with 35% of held splits by the team's longest. The report reaches more of the team on small maps (beacon reach 28-32% of dragon-turns on Default-like maps against 5-8% on Trauma), so the false-king share should be lower; count it. Measure first, on a debug copy against this champion and the swarm on 12 fresh small maps, both sides: held ordinary splits a game (the debug line's nosplit seed, which marks only splits the hold changed) and false kings a round. Stop only if held splits are under 0.1 a game with the 95% interval wholly below 0.1 (chance.rate_ci when under 10 events; on small maps the team may rarely reach its ceiling). Otherwise build and report per size band. Also count eliminations of ours against the champion's on the same map-sides (chance.sign_p): a rise at p <= 0.1 would mean units were lacking after all, and the hold should then also need no enemy head in the king's view.

title: The protected king treats tiles an enemy head can reach by a 2-step sprint as risky
hypothesis: Safety::riskyFor counts only 1-step enemy reach, but any dragon of length >= 3 can sprint 2 steps (L-1 steps allowed), and a head-to-head kills both regardless of length. In E0100 loss 0210-gen_eval_111406200-aA, our king 1024 (length 23, the team's longest by 5) moved S at r469 onto 35,27 while enemy 1047 (length 3-4, 3 tiles away) sprinted NN onto the same tile, and both died. Build: with Safety::protectedDragon (from mergeRound, our longest), riskyFor also flags tiles within 2 steps of an enemy head whose visible length is >= 3 and whose ram would be a bad trade (badRammer), using the same penalty. This only changes the king's moves, from mergeRound on. The evidence is one watched case: a rough count over the 40 loss replays found 38 of our near-longest dragons (length >= 10, from r300) dying with an enemy sprint within 3 tiles that round, against 30 for the opponent, which is no clear asymmetry. So count king deaths by 2-step sprint in candidate-vs-champion games first, and treat it as a low-priority SPRT. Scenarios: a length-20 king at r460 with a length-4 enemy head 2 tiles straight ahead avoids the tile between them; the same enemy at 3 tiles leaves the move alone; a non-king length-5 dragon behaves as today.

title: Tune the merge cascade: when it starts, when it stops, how close a merge partner must be
hypothesis: E0048's merge cascade (+30, kept) runs on first-guess numbers: mergeRound 300 (also the round ordinary splits stop and the king becomes protected), mergeMinUnits 8, mergeRadius 2, kingPearlReach 4, protectMinLength 6. About 55% of referee games are decided at round 500 on longest dragon (playbook), so these numbers set the tiebreak in most games. Leaders fold later than round 300: SSS's study replays keep their longest at 19-25 through r300-350 and fold mostly after r430 (133944: king 41 at r431 to 70 at r499), and they keep splitting late (late splits per game SSS 38, Sabotage-d 41, our 4219 20). Tune these 5 numbers together with SPSA (they decide one behaviour: when and how the swarm folds), then run the tuned values under the predeclared SPRT. Boundary: SPSA keeps signs and stays within 4x of the start (so mergeRound can move between 75 and 499 in principle; values past 480 turn the cascade off). Report the tuned values and longest/total at r499 in a few diagnostic games.

title: Corridor traffic: don't enter a 1-wide corridor that a known head is coming through from the far end
hypothesis: With E0050's tie-break-only out-of-sight term, dragons enter 1-wide corridors they can't see the end of, and the new deaths are traffic, not dead ends. In Devil self-play, deaths of dragons of length <= 3 within 10 rounds of entering a 1-wide corridor rose from 1 to 84 per game (2000 -> 5). Watched example: a length-2 dragon going north up Devil's 13-tile wrap-around corridor at x=8 met a length-4 teammate coming south; neither could turn round, so it hit the wall (c5 self-play, round 77). In a logging copy over 60 candidate-vs-champion games on near-ladder maps, dragons of length <= 3 on turns where 5 and 2000 chose different moves died within 10 rounds 40% of the time (hitWall 18%), against a 17% baseline (hitWall 4%); on those turns they also ate 1.29 pearls in the next 10 rounds against a 0.67 baseline. So the pearls are real and the deaths come from meeting other dragons. Build: when a move's destination is a 1-wide corridor tile (two kelp edges on opposite or adjacent sides), walk the corridor over known edges to its far mouth. If any other dragon's head (teammate or enemy, from current view or the belief map's fresh sightings) is inside it or within 2 steps of the far mouth and closer to it than we are to the far end, score the move as a closed pocket the corridor's length long (shortfallPerTile). Break teammate ties by id so exactly one of two teammates yields. Put it behind its own switch in params.hpp. Scenarios: a teammate head 5 tiles into the corridor facing us makes a length-2 dragon take the open move; an empty corridor is still entered for the pearl at its mouth; the lower-id teammate of two at opposite mouths enters and the other waits. Caveat: vision is 7x7, so a head more than 3 tiles in is seen only through memory or sonar; measure how often the guard fires on devil, trauma, schooltime and QoS before trusting it.

title: Re-check E0204's learned ram gate on small maps: the champion with P.ramModel off (the hand ram rule decides again)
hypothesis: sig 2026-09-28 asked what to do about the learned ram after the fit tool's refit (orch/fit-tool, 220 games, logging copy of 8f57a4e) found the ram gate's learned weights help on big maps and not on small ones: refit against the live gate, held-out generated games, >=2400 tiles +0.26 a decision (se 0.056), <=1024 tiles -0.02 (se 0.036); official small maps left out, Default -0.27 (se 0.09), Devil -0.08 (se 0.04). E0204's own SPRT gained only against the champion copy (0.556) and was level against the rest of the rotation. That refit was measured against the live learned gate, not the hand rule, so whether the live gate beats the hand rule on small maps is untested: this is that test. Build the current champion with P.ramModel false and nothing else; an ordinary gain test on fresh maps with a small-map mix (small 0.5). If the switched-off version is kept, the learned gate becomes conditional on map size (on only at 1152+ tiles) in a follow-up rather than deleted, since the big-map evidence favours it. Report ram swings per decision both ways by size band.
